e2e/a11y.spec.ts.what: The accessibility overview page lists the components with their scan results, and a right-to-left story really flips the page direction.

e2e/ai-assistant.spec.ts.what: The Assistant panel sends a prompt, shows it thinking, answers with a change that Undo takes back, and the Activity feed and scope chip work by keyboard.

e2e/alert-dialog.spec.ts.what: In the Alert dialog, type-to-confirm keeps the button off until the exact words are typed, and Cancel, Esc and focus return work.

e2e/app-provider.spec.ts.what: The App provider shows one toast at a time with its Undo, and draws every icon inside it at the same line weight.

e2e/backoffice.spec.ts.what: Every item in the back office's side navigation opens its own page without errors, and projects and phases open with the right tabs.

e2e/base.spec.ts.what: The Base intro page and each Base entry's docs page say what Base is, and Base sits last in the Storybook sidebar.

e2e/build-tab.spec.ts.what: On a phase's Build tab, the setup rows (access rights, participant actions, phone preview, notifications) open, change and undo by keyboard as expected.

e2e/charts.spec.ts.what: Line charts, sparklines and bar rows show the right values on hover, walk by arrow keys, and highlight the series under the pointer.

e2e/checks.spec.ts.what: Overview › Checks shows the last run, the four faults the break-it demo caught, and every guard with its rerun command.

e2e/comment-thread.spec.ts.what: In a Comment thread, Reply, Post, Delete with Undo and the internal tab all work, and Esc in a side panel keeps typed words.

e2e/community-monitor.spec.ts.what: The back office's Community monitor shows its health score, quarter picker, results by category and settings tabs, with no gaps left in the system.

e2e/component-page.spec.ts.what: A component's docs page shows its thirteen sections in order, each filled in, and a part named in bold links to its page; every part reaches the built Storybook with exactly one lifecycle stage tag, the one its page shows; a default from a part's words reads plainly in its Props table.

e2e/dashboard.spec.ts.what: The back office's Dashboard shows its sections, filters, cards and charts, and each tab has its own web address.

e2e/data-table-open.spec.ts.what: In the Data table, pressing a row opens it while ticks stay, the checkbox only ticks, and Shift ticks a range.

e2e/data-table-virtual.spec.ts.what: A Data table with 5,000 rows draws only a few at a time, scrolls under its header, walks by keyboard, and select-all ticks every row.

e2e/file-list.spec.ts.what: In the File list, Delete removes its file, one after another.

e2e/for-developers.spec.ts.what: The For developers page shows the developer guide to the reader, without the notes meant only for merging.

e2e/form-validation.spec.ts.what: Submitting a form with mistakes moves focus to the first field to fix, then the next, and every field shows its message.

e2e/forms.spec.ts.what: Date range field, Choice card, File list and Text field behave as designed: invalid end date message, Add end date, arrow keys, revealed content.

e2e/foundations.spec.ts.what: The Foundations pages (Colour, Typography, Size, Focus and states, Icons) show their tokens whole and in the right order in the sidebar.

e2e/illustrations.spec.ts.what: The Illustrations gallery shows every drawing grouped, shows still pictures under reduced motion, and the Empty state draws its notebook.

e2e/inputs.spec.ts.what: In the back office's Input manager, filters, sorting and search narrow the inputs, and a row opens in a Side panel with undoable status changes.

e2e/inspiration-hub.spec.ts.what: The back office's Inspiration hub shows highlighted and all projects with filters, pages of six cards, copy with Undo, and a preview.

e2e/layout.spec.ts.what: Grid, Stack and Inline lay parts out as designed: 16 apart, a list beside its detail, wrapping topics, and fields spanning all columns.

e2e/locale-toolbar.spec.ts.what: Switching the Storybook language shows German or Dutch numbers and months and right-to-left Arabic, while the words stay English.

e2e/map.spec.ts.what: The Map draws with credits and no network use, pins are keyboard-reachable buttons that open cards, and zoom and list hover work.

e2e/menu.spec.ts.what: In a multiple-choice Menu with a footer action, Enter and Space tick items and keep it open, and the action closes it.

e2e/messaging.spec.ts.what: The back office's Messaging screens (custom emails, automated emails, SMS) list, switch, compose and send as the real admin does.

e2e/motion.spec.ts.what: The Motion page lists the motion tokens, the Modal moves on them, and under reduced motion the durations collapse while the Modal still works.

e2e/multilingual-text-field.spec.ts.what: The Multilingual text field switches language by keyboard, fills only that language, flags a missing required one, and runs Arabic right to left.

e2e/official-update.spec.ts.what: In the Official update form, Publish stays off until there are words, publishing can be undone, and the bulk Modal returns focus.

e2e/orientation.spec.ts.what: The orientation and developer pages render their sections, and Welcome links to every one of them.

e2e/pages-menu.spec.ts.what: The back office's Pages and menu screen orders menu items, switches pages, asks before deleting and opens the editors.

e2e/pages.spec.ts.what: A project's Build, Manage and Phases rail screens show the setup cards and selectable inputs, and move between phases.

e2e/paint.spec.ts.what: Primary, secondary and quiet buttons and the select trigger wear the colours the Figma design gives them.

e2e/play.spec.ts.what: Every story that acts itself out (the keyboard tables cite them) plays to its end without a failed step; a short list known to fail today may only shrink.

e2e/project-overview.spec.ts.what: A project's overview has its own address and three columns, shows the live phase and next actions, and keeps the publish checklist for drafts.

e2e/project-phase.spec.ts.what: A phase's Manage and Build tabs list ideas with metrics and filters, select rows, and pass the accessibility check.

e2e/projects.spec.ts.what: The back office's Projects list shows views, filters, a full table, paging, row menus, and the New project flow.

e2e/report-parts.spec.ts.what: The report builder's parts: Page stage zooms, fits and follows the page in view, the Zoom bar stops at its ends and speaks the locale, and the block, text, figure, quote and sortable parts work by role and keyboard.

e2e/report-view.spec.ts.what: The back office's report view has outline, pages and assistant; selecting, keyboard use and block edits with Undo all work.

e2e/reporting.spec.ts.what: The back office's Reporting list searches, edits, duplicates and deletes reports, and creating a report starts blank and opens the report view.

e2e/seams.spec.ts.what: The integration seam recipes (a router link, a form library, translated words, data that loads and fails) each play through.

e2e/segmented-control.spec.ts.what: The Segmented control puts icons before its words, and its unread dot says what it means on hover and focus.

e2e/selectors.spec.ts.what: Select, Option list, Tag picker and Setup step choose, tick and remove options correctly by keyboard, and say when nothing is found.

e2e/settings.spec.ts.what: The back office's Settings has its seven tabs, a multilingual platform name, Save that waits for a change, and undoable switches.

e2e/side-panel.spec.ts.what: The Side panel opens with focus inside, keeps its 560 or 440 width, closes by Esc or the close button, and returns focus to the row.

e2e/sidebar.spec.ts.what: The back office's side navigation lists items in the real order, shows the count badge, and opens notifications and the account menu.

e2e/site.spec.ts.what: The landing page links both the Storybook and the back office and is hidden from search, and a story renders.

e2e/stat-tile.spec.ts.what: A Stat tile says its trend direction in words, not colour alone, and its info icon opens a Help popover by press and keyboard.

e2e/stories.spec.ts.what: Every story in the built Storybook opens without breaking.

e2e/table.spec.ts.what: The table toolbar's collapsible search, Pagination and caret keys work by keyboard, and a table in a panel updates its count.

e2e/tabs.spec.ts.what: Tabs include a count and status dot in their name, and grouped side tabs skip headings and let arrow keys cross groups.

e2e/tools.spec.ts.what: The back office's Tools page shows one card per tool; tokens, webhooks and the Esri key can be created, edited and deleted with a confirmation.

e2e/users.spec.ts.what: In the back office's Users tab, 5,000 people scroll in one list, and select-all ticks them all.

tests/a11y.test.mjs.what: The accessibility overview groups problems by component, worst first, keeps where each one is on the page, and says which colour palette was checked.

tests/api-report.test.mjs.what: The written list of every public name and component option is up to date, so any API change shows as a change developers can review.

tests/backoffice-motion.test.mjs.what: The back office stylesheet uses the motion tokens for every speed and easing, never raw values.

tests/backoffice-places.test.mjs.what: The back office's own styles may only place things (where, how big, how far apart), never colour, type, borders or shadows; the paint list only shrinks.

tests/card.test.mjs.what: The Card is outlined unless filled, shows media first, shows review status and menu values as a pill, and can be placed by the page.

tests/checks-page.test.mjs.what: Overview › Checks says in plain words what every guard proves, and its break-it run shows all four faults caught.

tests/component-pages.test.mjs.what: Every component page that is written has all its sections, each 'use instead' names a real part, and interactive parts have a keyboard table.

tests/components-described.test.mjs.what: Every component and pattern has a one-line description in the component list, and none is left marked as not yet described.

tests/components-index.test.mjs.what: The component list and the site's text index for AI readers match the stories, so a changed story or doc comment is never missed.

tests/copy.test.mjs.what: Docs page headings are in sentence case, and no page uses a word the word list says to avoid.

tests/css-scope.test.mjs.what: Base's styles only paint the system's own parts, so an app's own React Aria elements keep the look the app gives them.

tests/data-table.test.mjs.what: The Data table's select-all, its row heights for long lists, and the invented people in the long-list stories give the expected numbers.

tests/date-range-field.test.mjs.what: The Date range field reads dates as year-month-day text, offers Add end date, and calls an end before the start invalid in words.

tests/defaults.test.mjs.what: A default written from a part's own words shows in the Props table as plain text (labels.filters ("Active filters")), without the backticks and escaped quotes Storybook would leave.

tests/figma-spec.test.mjs.what: Looking up a component for its Figma spec finds it by its last name, prefers an exact match, and never matches a variant or part of a name.

tests/gv-chart.test.mjs.what: Charts pick round axis steps, describe trends and single points in plain words in the viewer's number format, and find the nearest point.

tests/icons-documented.test.mjs.what: The Icons page lists every icon the components and the back office actually use.

tests/illustrations.test.mjs.what: Each illustration is one self-contained drawing painted only with tokens, with motion only from the motion tokens, and named and sized in the agreed format.

tests/layout-parts.test.mjs.what: Stack, Inline and Grid turn their gap, padding, columns and areas into the right spacing tokens and nothing else, and stay placeable by the page.

tests/layout-text.test.mjs.what: Text, Visually hidden, Page header and Tile grid draw the right element, heading level, defaults and kind or colour.

tests/lifecycle.test.mjs.what: Every component and pattern carries exactly one lifecycle stage (draft, candidate or stable), and it is the stage the written rule gives from the repo's facts; nothing is stable before a developer has reviewed it.

tests/map.test.mjs.what: The Map fits its pins into view, groups nearby pins as it zooms, moves between pins by arrow keys, and places the card and credits line correctly.

tests/menu-icons.test.mjs.what: Back office menu items put their icon in the Menu's icon slot, so it sits before the words instead of after them.

tests/motion.test.mjs.what: Every speed and easing in the stylesheets comes from a motion token, and every endless animation stops under reduced motion.

tests/multiloc.test.mjs.what: The language switcher knows which languages are filled, empty, required or invalid, keeps the platform order, runs Arabic, Hebrew, Persian and Urdu right to left, and names languages.

tests/no-css-in-js.test.mjs.what: No styled-components or similar code-based styling is installed or imported anywhere; all styling stays in stylesheets using tokens.

tests/no-names.test.mjs.what: No file in the repo names a person, the site or the docs; they say Figma, the prototype or the designer instead.

tests/no-outer-margin.test.mjs.what: No component sets space outside itself; the page that places it owns the space, and the short list of exceptions only shrinks.

tests/own-block.test.mjs.what: A component's stylesheet only styles its own parts, so a change inside Badge cannot silently change the Data table; the exceptions list only shrinks.

tests/pagination.test.mjs.what: Pagination shows every page up to seven, then keeps seven slots with first, last and an ellipsis, always including the current page.

tests/paint.test.mjs.what: Every colour in the stylesheets comes from a token: no raw colours, no named colours, no dark-mode blocks, and the token font is used.

tests/react-aria-table.test.mjs.what: The table of what comes from React Aria matches the code, part by part.

tests/rename-tokens.test.mjs.what: The tool that renames old token names in stylesheets renames only whole names, splits by what is painted, snaps spaces to the scale, and flags the rest.

tests/side-panel.test.mjs.what: The Side panel opens as the page says, takes its preset width, and its record head shows the title as a heading, Posted by, date and actions.

tests/sidebar-public.test.mjs.what: Entries that exist only for a test stay out of the public Storybook sidebar.

tests/system-first.test.mjs.what: The back office builds only from the design system's public entry points, borrows no story data beyond a short list, and has one layout-only stylesheet.

tests/tabs.test.mjs.what: A Tab panel placed outside Tab panels warns developers, and a caller's own class is added to Tabs, never replacing the system's.

tests/toast.test.mjs.what: A toast carries a title and description for 5 seconds by default, can take an action, icon and timeout, and the App provider draws no markup of its own.

tests/token-names.test.mjs.what: Every token name follows the naming rules, with no colour names outside colour and chart tokens and no component names outside the side navigation.

tests/token-usage.test.mjs.what: The map of which tokens each component uses is worked out correctly from the stylesheets.

tests/tokens-defined.test.mjs.what: Every token a file uses really exists; a guessed or retired token name fails here instead of showing as a missing colour in a browser.

tests/tokens-only.test.mjs.what: Every space, radius, text size, line height, weight and shadow in the stylesheets comes from a token, and only the base-4 steps are used.

tests/tokens.test.mjs.what: The tokens are read from the Figma foundations correctly: names follow Figma, colours, type, space and shadows are kept, and clashing names are refused.

tests/words.test.mjs.what: No component carries its own words or fixed language: every word comes from the page or editable labels, and numbers and dates follow the viewer's locale.
